assessment:
The table watches you cast a tutor and starts counting Dragons. Let them count.

Three of your four wishes are not shopping for a Dragon at all. They are shopping for the enchantment that turns one Dragon into the whole night, and you should be honest with yourself about that before you spend one.

Know the delivery before you cast. Sarkhan's Triumph and Tiamat hand you the card; Enlightened Tutor and Worldly Tutor put it on top, so buy on the turn before you need it and never on the turn you need it.

Check your board first, because two cards delete that wait. With Korlessa, Scale Singer out you cast Dragons off the top of your library, and Herald's Horn's upkeep peek puts a topped Dragon straight into your hand. Look, then decide whether the wish costs you a turn at all.

Every fetch here is revealed, so treat the wish as an announcement and time it like one. Buy the kill piece the turn before you swing. Buy it two turns early and you are just telling the table which permanent to kill.

Now the funding law, and it has cost pilots games. Haven of the Spirit Dragon, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, Unclaimed Territory, Rivaz of the Claw and an attacking Klauth all make spells-only mana — spend it on the tutors themselves, because a tutor is a spell, and never on Aggravated Assault's {3}{R}{R}. That is an activated ability and restricted mana cannot touch it.

So count lands, rocks and Treasures before you declare attackers, not after.

And stop wishing toward your commander. He lands on turn nine on average and not once by turn six across ten thousand goldfished games — aim every wish at the turn you actually take instead.

targets.scenario: End step of the turn before your pivot. Old Gnawbone or Savage Ventmaw is already on the battlefield, you can produce five unrestricted mana next turn, and nothing in your hand ends the game.
targets.why: Spend one white mana and buy the exit. Draw it, cast it, and you are standing inside a signed kill: Ventmaw's attack trigger overpays the reactivation by a mana every cycle (stack 003), and Gnawbone banks two net Treasures per unblocked cycle and takes opponents down one at a time (stack 006). Pay the {3}{R}{R} from lands, rocks and Treasures only — your spells-only sources will not pay an activation, so recount before you attack. The reveal tells the table what is coming, so make this the turn before you win.

targets.scenario: Turn two or three. Your hand is six- and seven-drops, your board is two lands, and nothing has cost less than five since the mulligan.
targets.why: Buy the discount, not the payoff. You draw a cost reducer by turn six in only 33.2% of games, so two games in three you have to go and get one — make this the wish that fixes the hand you actually have. Incubator on top of eminence takes {3} off every Dragon, which drops your whole top shelf into range turns early. One mana for the deck's rarest resource is the best behind-fetch on the sheet.

targets.scenario: Mid-game. Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks or Scourge of Valkas is already down, and the expensive half of your hand is stranded behind your land count.
targets.why: Stop paying for Dragons and start renting them. One red apiece, haste attached, every enters- and attacks-trigger live, and the damage stays after the end-step sacrifice — stack 005 put Drakuseth's 17 on the record at that price. It is an enchantment, so park it before the wrath, not after.

targets.scenario: Miirym is on the battlefield and has survived a rotation. The table has priced your doubling and moved on.
targets.why: Take the wish nobody plays around. Stack 002 ran the cascade: Miirym, Panharmonicon, Terror of the Peaks and Dragon Tempest down, one Lathliss cast, two extra Lathlisses and 64 damage across twelve targeted triggers — so cast the artifact on the quiet turn and hold your next Dragon for the loud one. Nobody reads a four-mana artifact as a kill until it has already happened.

tutors.notes: This one tops your library, so it costs you a draw step — cast it at the end of the turn before you want the card and you pay nothing extra. The reveal is public: fetch Aggravated Assault and every experienced seat now knows your plan, so hold Deflecting Swat as the bodyguard on that turn rather than deploying it.

targets.scenario: Aggravated Assault is on the battlefield or in hand, you can fund the activation from Treasures or untapped lands, and you want the other half tonight.
targets.why: Take the half that pays for itself twice. Instant speed, straight to hand, one cast from the verified table-kill — Gnawbone plus Assault banks two net Treasures per unblocked cycle and kills opponents sequentially, combats six and twelve in the resolved game (stack 006). His Treasures are unrestricted, which is exactly the mana your Dragon-only lands cannot make, so this fetch answers the funding problem and the kill in one card.

targets.scenario: Assault is live but your mana is thin — you get one Dragon down this turn and nothing else.
targets.why: Take the cheaper engine half when the mana is tight. Ventmaw's attack trigger adds {R}{R}{R}{G}{G}{G}, which covers the {3}{R}{R} with a mana spare — the loop gains a mana every cycle rather than costing one (stack 003). You need exactly one clean combat, so pick the seat that cannot block and go.

targets.scenario: You expect a damage-based sweeper next rotation, or you are holding Blasphemous Act yourself.
targets.why: Get him down before the sweep and the sweeper becomes their mistake. Stack 004 verified Blasphemous Act into three of your Dragons throwing 39 at one opponent's face, the triggers resolving from beyond the grave. Respect the boundary out loud: destroy-all and exile-all effects deal no damage and feed him nothing, so keep playing around those. The instant-speed Sneak Attack ambush version has no stack behind it — do not build a turn on it.

targets.scenario: The table has priced you off a nine-mana commander and stopped watching your combat step. You have six mana.
targets.why: Rent the commander instead of buying him. Courser's entry puts The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield with haste for one attack, so you get a card per attacking Dragon and a free permanent from hand, and he goes home at end step with no tax accrued — stack 005 names Courser as the cheat that actually works here. Cast him on the turn you are already attacking and skip nine mana entirely.

tutors.notes: Dragon creature cards only — this never finds Aggravated Assault, Sneak Attack or an artifact, so stop reaching for it when the missing piece is a permanent that does not fly. Three mana at instant speed means you shop on somebody else's end step and keep your entire turn for the cast.

targets.scenario: The standard cast, turn six through eight. Eminence brings her down a mana, your board is stable, and you are buying the endgame. Take five names: Old Gnawbone, Savage Ventmaw, Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm, Dragonlord Kolaghan and Hellkite Courser.
targets.why: Load the package so every draw completes something. Gnawbone and Ventmaw are both Assault partners — the table-kill and the self-funding loop (stacks 006 and 003) — so whichever one you draw first ends the game. Miirym doubles every Dragon after her (stack 002), Kolaghan hastes the wave so it attacks the turn it lands, and Courser rents your commander for an attack with no tax (stack 005). Take the whole shelf and stop rationing.

targets.scenario: Against the wall. Your board is swept, your life is under pressure, and two seats are ahead of you on tempo. Take Dragonlord Dromoka, Wrathful Red Dragon, Atsushi, the Blazing Sky, Goldspan Dragon and Drakuseth, Maw of Flames.
targets.why: Trade speed for certainty here and take every card that defends, refunds or removes. Dromoka is uncounterable, gains you life and shuts opponents out of casting on your turn, so your rebuild actually resolves. Wrathful makes their next damage sweeper a 39-point mistake (stack 004), Atsushi dies forward into three unrestricted Treasures that legally pay Assault, Goldspan brings haste and Treasure per attack, and Drakuseth is a removal spell that attacks for 10 before blockers. Climb back on cards that cannot lose you more ground.

tutors.notes: Two laws, and breaking either wastes a nine-drop. Her trigger reads 'if you cast it' — a Sneak Attack'd Tiamat or a Miirym copy searches for nothing, so hard-cast her every single time. And the five must be Dragon cards with different names, none of them Tiamat, so pick the package before you cast rather than at the table.

targets.scenario: Turn three or four, one green open at an opponent's end step, and your engine wants its multiplier before it wants a body.
targets.why: Buy the doubler first and everything after it arrives twice. Every nontoken Dragon you cast from that point brings a token copy, and under Panharmonicon she triggers twice per Dragon (stack 002). If Korlessa, Scale Singer is already out, the card never even touches your hand — you cast it off the top, so check for her before you count the transit turn.

targets.scenario: Aggravated Assault is on the battlefield with Treasures or untapped lands ready to pay {3}{R}{R} after your next draw.
targets.why: One green at instant speed sets up the whole table-kill: draw Gnawbone, cast him, connect once, and the engine banks two net Treasures per cycle while opponents fall in order (stack 006). No other one-mana spell in this deck buys an endgame, so when the board is that close, take it and stop looking for a better use.

targets.scenario: Sneak Attack is down, a payoff is out, and you need damage this turn rather than development next turn.
targets.why: Buy the exchange rate stack 005 already priced: one red puts Drakuseth in with haste, and 17 damage — four plus three plus three off the trigger, seven more in combat — stands after the end-step sacrifice. Turn any dead topdeck into that line for a single green mana and pick your target before you cast, not after.

tutors.notes: It reveals and it sits on top, so cast it at the last legal moment and let the table price your draw step wrong. Herald's Horn's upkeep peek pulls a topped Dragon into hand for free, and Korlessa lets you cast it straight off the library — with either one down this wish is effectively instant.

gaps: No wish reaches the graveyard. Patriarch's Bidding is a mass rebuy, not a search, so once a key Dragon is exiled nothing here brings it back — play around exile removal rather than planning to recover from it.

Enlightened Tutor is the only search in the 99 that finds Aggravated Assault, and all three contained infinites route through that one enchantment. One tutor of redundancy is thin cover for a single point of failure, so land that wish with protection already in hand.
The Cavern-Hoard Dragon pairing with Assault has no stack behind it. Fetch Gnawbone or Ventmaw when you are buying a kill, and treat Cavern-Hoard as Treasures until the checker says otherwise.
Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon can sacrifice for a Dragon to hand, but it is a land — its story belongs to Sources Say. Count it when you plan your mana, not when you plan a wish.
